title: Twelve, seven, five
hook: Twelver Shia follow twelve Imams, Isma'ilis a different line after Ja'far, Zaydis another after Ali Zayn al-Abidin

segments.voice: Yesterday: al-Baqir and his son Ja'far al-Sadiq, a father and son teaching in a Medina courtyard. Your line was the splitting-open of knowledge.

A family tree has a way of forking. Two brothers, two inheritances, two sets of cousins who each tell the story from their own branch. The Shia line of Imams forked too, more than once, and the forks have names. Outsiders sometimes call them by numbers: Twelvers, Seveners, Fivers. Those nicknames are rough, and the communities have their own names for themselves. But the numbers open a question Shia Muslims had to answer more than once: when an Imam dies, which son carries the line?
screen: `A FAMILY TREE FORKS.` → `TWELVERS, SEVENERS, FIVERS.` → `WHICH SON CARRIES THE LINE?`

segments.voice: All three tell their story back through Ali and Fatima, Hasan and Husayn. The first fork comes after Husayn's son Ali Zayn al-Abidin, al-Sajjad. One of his sons, Zayd, rose up in Kufa against the Umayyads and was killed. Those who held that an Imam is any descendant of Hasan or Husayn who stands up openly against injustice followed Zayd's example. They are the Zaydis, and because Zayd comes fifth when the line is counted from Ali, outsiders call them Fivers. Zaydi communities live in Yemen today. Others held that the line had already passed from Zayn al-Abidin to Zayd's brother, Muhammad al-Baqir, and then to Ja'far al-Sadiq. The second fork comes after Ja'far. Some held that the line passed through his son Isma'il and Isma'il's son. They are the Isma'ilis, sometimes called Seveners. Isma'ili communities today have their own branches, and some follow a living Imam, present in the world now. Others followed Ja'far's son Musa, called al-Kazim, the one who holds back his anger, and the line went on, father to son, to a twelfth Imam. These are the Twelvers, the Ithna Ashariyya, the Shia of Iran, Iraq, Lebanon and beyond, whose law, as yesterday said, is called Ja'fari. Each line holds that it kept faith with the Prophet's family, peace be upon him. Each has its own scholars, its own prayers, its own sense of what an Imam is. None of them is a footnote to another. Three lines of imams.
screen: `THE FIRST FORK: AFTER ZAYN AL-ABIDIN.` · `ZAYD: THE ZAYDIS.` · `ISMA'IL: THE ISMA'ILIS.` · `MUSA, TO THE TWELFTH: THE TWELVERS.` · then, large: `THREE LINES OF IMAMS.`

segments.voice: Say the three names slowly in your head: Zaydi, Isma'ili, Ithna Ashari, Twelver. Pick one you hadn't heard before and hold it the way you'd hold a new neighbor's name, wanting to get it right. Wonder what you'd like to know about the people who carry it, and keep the question, not an answer.
Twelve. The Twelver Shia line of Imams, from Ali to the twelfth, beside the Isma'ili and Zaydi lines that forked from it. Today's word.
Your line: three lines of imams. Shia Muslims are more than one community. Rest well.

howItsDone: Twelver, Isma'ili and Zaydi Shia Muslims each honor their own line of Imams descended from Ali and Fatima; some Isma'ili communities follow a living Imam today.

chat.says: Are all Shia Muslims one single group?
options: No. Twelvers, Isma'ilis and Zaydis each follow their own line of Imams.
Yes. Every Shia Muslim today follows the very same twelve Imams.
No, but they only differ about the first Imam, not later ones.
chat.meaning: The line forked: Zaydis after Zayn al-Abidin, Isma'ilis after Ja'far, and Twelvers through Musa al-Kazim to a twelfth Imam.

Zaydis.meaning: Shia who followed Zayd's example; Fivers to outsiders

Isma'ilis.meaning: Shia whose line passed through Ja'far's son Isma'il

al-Kazim.meaning: the one who holds back his anger; Musa, Ja'far's son

Ithna Ashariyya.meaning: the Twelvers, Shia who follow twelve Imams

Ja'fari.meaning: Twelver Shia law, named after Ja'far al-Sadiq

notes: 'Zaydi communities have lived for centuries in Yemen': confirm phrasing.
'Some Isma'ili communities follow a living Imam' (the Nizari Imam); Musta'li/Bohra communities hold their Imam is in seclusion. Confirm the brief framing is fair.
Isma'ilis: the script says the line passed 'through his son Isma'il and Isma'il's son' (Muhammad ibn Isma'il); confirm.
al-Kazim glossed as 'the one who holds back his anger'; confirm.
'The Shia of Iran, Iraq, Lebanon and beyond' for Twelvers: a geographic description, no counts; confirm.
Index word is 'Twelve' (title head); kept exactly.

Audit: 'all three lines trace back through Zayn al-Abidin' was wrong for Zaydis (the Zaydi imamate is open to any descendant of Hasan or Husayn who rises, and the Yemeni Zaydi imams were largely Hasanid), so the teach, a screen head and myth 2 now say the first fork comes after Zayn al-Abidin; 'the rest followed Zayd's brother al-Baqir' implied the Imamis chose al-Baqir after Zayd's revolt, when for them he had succeeded his father decades earlier; reworded.

Editor: 'all three lines share the first four Imams' was not fair to Zaydi and Isma'ili counts (Zaydis do not generally count Zayn al-Abidin as an Imam; Nizari Isma'ilis count Hasan differently), so the teach, a screen head and the second myth item now speak of descent through Zayn al-Abidin instead; 'Zayd comes fifth in their count' became 'fifth when the line is counted from Ali'; uncited 'for centuries' cut.
